notes.ennyanja: Un lac; beware: la mer is the sea.
notes.omugga: Une rivière; a big river reaching the sea is un fleuve.
notes.okukuuma: Protéger: protégeons, with an e to keep the g soft.

guidebook.intro: Lakes, rivers, forests and hills, and caring for the land. French uses “let’s” forms and superlatives for nature’s records.

tips.title: Plantons des arbres !
body: For “let’s”, use the **nous** form without **nous**: **Plantons des arbres ! Protégeons notre terre !** The negative: **Ne jetons pas de déchets.**
To one person: **Ne jette pas de déchets ici !**

tips.title: La plus haute montagne
body: “The most” or “the -est” is **le plus** / **la plus** + adjective: **la plus haute montagne d’Afrique** (the highest mountain in Africa), **le plus grand lac**. “In” after a superlative is **de**: **d’Afrique**.
**Le fleuve** is a river that flows into the sea, like the Nile; **la rivière** flows into another river or a lake.

culture.title: The Congo rainforest
body: The Congo Basin holds the world’s second-largest rainforest, **la forêt du bassin du Congo**, home to gorillas, bonobos and okapis. Protecting it is a big topic in the francophone news.
